# Kyoto Family Trip Plan for April 2026

A relaxed 4-day Kyoto plan for 2 adults + 1 child, shaped around temples, food markets, and easy walks, with lower-crowd alternatives and short transit times. Budget target: **¥180,000 total excluding flights**.

# 4-Day Itinerary With Costs and Meals

## Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive in Kyoto, check in, and keep the first half-day light with a slow walk around **Maruyama Park** and the quieter lanes near **Kodai-ji**.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and stroll toward **Ninenzaka/Sannenzaka** early evening before peak crowds.
- **Food:** Late lunch at a small soba or udon shop; dinner near Gion with tofu dishes, grilled fish, or a family-friendly set meal.
- **Estimated cost:** Lodging ¥18,000; meals ¥9,000; local transport ¥2,000; entry/snacks ¥3,000; **Day total ¥32,000**.

## Day 2: Temples and Gentle Garden Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Start at **Kiyomizu-dera** right at opening, then continue to **Entoku-in** or a nearby temple garden for a calmer pace.
- **Afternoon:** Head to **Nanzen-ji** and the **Philosopher’s Path** for an easy walk; keep the route short and stop whenever the child needs a break.
- **Food:** Breakfast at the hotel or a bakery; lunch with yuba, rice bowls, or curry; dinner in the Okazaki/Higashiyama area to avoid a long return trip.
- **Estimated cost:** Lodging ¥18,000; meals ¥10,000; transport ¥2,500; entry ¥4,000; **Day total ¥34,500**.

## Day 3: Markets, Crafts, and Riverside Strolls
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Nishiki Market** early for a quieter food-market experience; focus on tasting rather than shopping heavily.
- **Afternoon:** Walk along the **Kamo River** and spend time around **Demachiyanagi** or **Shimogamo Shrine** for a slower, less crowded afternoon.
- **Food:** Market snacks for lunch; tea and sweets in the afternoon; dinner with Kyoto-style obanzai or a simple tempura set.
- **Estimated cost:** Lodging ¥18,000; meals ¥11,000; transport ¥2,000; snacks/market tasting ¥5,000; **Day total ¥36,000**.

## Day 4: Arashiyama Early, Then Easy Exit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Go to **Arashiyama** very early and keep the visit focused on **Tenryu-ji** and the riverside area before crowds build.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one easy add-on only: the **Okochi Sanso Garden** or a short bamboo grove walk, then return to the hotel to pack.
- **Food:** Early breakfast, a simple noodle or tofu lunch in Arashiyama, and a final Kyoto-style dinner near your stay or station.
- **Estimated cost:** Lodging ¥18,000; meals ¥10,000; transport ¥3,000; entry ¥4,000; **Day total ¥35,000**.

## Budget Snapshot
| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---:|
| Lodging | ¥72,000 |
| Meals | ¥40,000 |
| Local transport | ¥9,500 |
| Entry fees | ¥15,000 |
| Snacks/market tasting | ¥8,000 |
| Buffer for extras | ¥12,000 |
| **Trip total** | **¥156,500** |

## Best Fit for Your Preferences
- **Temple-heavy but calm:** Kiyomizu-dera early, Nanzen-ji, Shimogamo Shrine, Tenryu-ji
- **Food-market focus:** Nishiki Market early in the day, plus Kyoto-style dinners
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Food-market focus:** Nishiki Market early in the day, plus Kyoto-style dinners, Kyoto, Japan
- **Easy walking:** Philosopher’s Path, Kamo River, Maruyama Park, Arashiyama riverside
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Easy walking:** Philosopher’s Path, Kamo River, Maruyama Park, Arashiyama riverside, Kyoto, Japan
- **Crowd control:** Start major sights at opening, avoid midday peak at Arashiyama and Higashiyama, keep one major stop per half-day

# Packing Checklist for Kyoto in April

## Spring Travel Essentials
- Light waterproof jacket or compact umbrella
- Layered tops: T-shirts, long sleeves, light sweater
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- Socks you can easily remove for temple visits
- Small day bag for water, snacks, and wipes
- Portable charger and charging cable
- Reusable water bottle
- Tissue pack and hand sanitizer
- Sun protection: hat, sunscreen, sunglasses
- Light scarf or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Child essentials: snacks, small activity item, spare layers, motion-sickness medicine if needed
- Cash in small denominations for markets and small shops

## Useful Notes for April Weather
- Kyoto in April is usually mild, but mornings and evenings can still feel cool.
- Occasional rain is common, so pack one rain layer rather than a heavy coat.
- Temple areas often require more walking than they first appear, so prioritize comfort over style.
